inputs.prompt:
Image 1 is an authoritative vertical 9:16 overhead city-map layout guide. Repaint this exact layout as one polished winter production illustration while preserving the positions and count of its elements. Keep the regular city street grid, perpendicular intersections, crosswalks, railway line, public park, sports block, small residential and office blocks, and exactly one broad central blue logistics center with its loading court. Do not turn it into a single warehouse diorama, a snowy field, a 3/4 landscape, or a generic new map. Image 2 is a production artwork reference for surface language only: borrow tactile paper grain, hand-painted contours, snow and asphalt texture, practical carrier silhouettes, and the accepted blue-white-orange winter palette. Do not copy Image 2's composition.

The four colored vehicle silhouettes in Image 1 are mandatory anchors. Repaint exactly four and only four complete delivery vehicles at those four locations, with no traffic, duplicates, detached trailers, cropped fragments, or extra cars: a small old muted truck at the upper-left inspection road; a medium compact distinctive utility delivery truck directly beside the central logistics center's right-side loading/office exit; a blue crew truck on the lower-left wide perimeter road with exactly two separate adult drivers readable through the cab; and a modern bright-orange Express truck on the lower-right outer arterial. Keep vehicles small enough to belong to the map, but clearly readable at 375 px; the near truck is larger than the old truck, crew is the largest, and Express is slightly smaller than crew. The near truck must not duplicate the old or crew silhouette: use a short cab-over utility body with a compact raised cargo box, dark teal cab, pale body, and no writing.

Make the map feel alive through visible cause and effect, not decorative clutter. OLD is moving slowly from a distant inspection post with faded paint, a very thin exhaust wisp and narrow tracks. NEAR is just leaving the loading court, with front wheels turned into a tight turn, a barrier and snow bank pinching its exit, brake/contact shadow, and short compressed ruts. CREW is traveling continuously around the broad perimeter road; its two drivers are distinct and its tracks continue behind it. EXPRESS is already moving fastest on the open arterial, with subtle radial blur inside the wheels, rear-tire powder spray, and the longest low tapered snow wake. Use only restrained painterly motion traces, no comic speed lines, glow, arrows, smoke clouds, or decorative noise.

Preserve the exact overhead city-map view, central logistics center, road connections, vertical distribution, and four anchor positions from Image 1. Use slightly dimensional painted building roofs and snow banks, but keep the camera close to bird's-eye so the map reads instantly. Do not add UI, labels, route overlays, pins, circles, ads, numbers, logos, or readable text anywhere except the single Express word directly on the orange cargo body. No photorealism, glossy 3D, low-poly toy style, or collage edges.
